absent: Locking, concurrency and ordering rules for floppy chaining, mapping queries, filter attachment and request handling.
Error codes, retry, timeout, reset and interrupt wait behavior beyond flag names.
System call and ioctl dispatch numbers for mapping, filter attach and device transport.
Memory ownership and copy semantics between user and kernel buffers and splice or zero copy paths.
State machines for motor control, directory offsets, lock negotiation, and forget versus destroy lifetimes.
Version negotiation and compatibility handling implied by compat sizes and minor version.

findings.text: The floppy raw command record begins with a flag word and continues with a user data address plus a kernel data address and a link used to chain commands inside the kernel. Transfer accounting follows as a remaining length, a physical length that may differ, and an allocated buffer length, then a rate byte and a command byte count. The command and reply area has two views, one with separate command bytes plus a reply count plus reply bytes and one flat view covering the whole area. The tail carries a track number, a numeric result, and two reserved integers.

Raw floppy control values are read one, write two, no motor four, disk change four with output meaning, interrupt wait eight, spin up sixteen, motor off after thirty two, need disk sixty four, need seek one hundred twenty eight, more records two hundred fifty six, stop on failure five hundred twelve, stop on success one thousand twenty four, soft failure two thousand forty eight, command failure sixty five thousand five hundred thirty six, and hard failure one hundred thirty one thousand seventy two.

The raw command area holds sixteen command bytes and sixteen reply bytes, with a combined full size of thirty three that accounts for command bytes plus one count byte plus reply bytes. Presence of a batch raw command marker indicates batched raw command support.
Three floppy controls are exposed on numeric type two with operation numbers hex fifty eight for raw command, hex fifty nine for twaddle, and hex five A for eject.

An extent record carries logical address, physical address and length as wide values, followed by two reserved wide values, a flag word, and three reserved narrow values. A mapping request header carries start and length as wide values, a flag word, a filled count of mapped extents, a capacity count, one reserved word, and a trailing variable length array of extent records.

Mapping request options are sync one, extended attribute tree two, and extent caching four, with a compatibility mask combining sync and extended attribute. The maximum representable offset is all bits set in a wide unsigned value.

Extent status bits are last one, unknown two, delayed allocation four, encoded eight, encrypted one hundred twenty eight, not aligned two hundred fifty six, inline data five hundred twelve, tail packing one thousand twenty four, unwritten two thousand forty eight, merged four thousand ninety six, and shared eight thousand one hundred ninety two. Delayed allocation implies unknown, inline and tail imply not aligned, encoded means unreadable while unmounted, encrypted and merged and shared describe protection, synthesis and sharing.

A classic filter cell holds a sixteen bit operation code, an eight bit true jump distance, an eight bit false jump distance, and a thirty two bit generic operand. A program header holds a sixteen bit cell count and a user address pointing at the cell array for socket attachment.

Classic filter version is major one minor one with sixteen scratch memory words. Result selection masks the operation code with hex eighteen where accumulator selection is hex ten. Miscellaneous operation selection masks with hex F eight where transfer to index is zero and transfer to accumulator is hex eighty. One constructor makes a non jump cell from code and operand, another makes a jump cell from code, operand and both jump distances.

Ancillary data access is anchored at negative four thousand ninety six, with protocol at zero, packet type at four, interface index at eight, netlink attribute at twelve, nested attribute at sixteen, mark at twenty, queue at twenty four, hardware type at twenty eight, receive hash at thirty two, cpu at thirty six, xor with index at forty, vlan tag at forty four, vlan presence at forty eight, payload offset at fifty two, random at fifty six, vlan protocol at sixty, and end marker at sixty four. Packet relative bases are network at negative ten forty eight thousand five hundred seventy six and link at negative twenty ninety seven thousand one hundred fifty two, each mirrored by a packet filter alias with equal value.

The filesystem attribute record starts with inode number, size and block count, then access, modification and change times as seconds, then three nanosecond parts, then mode, link count, user, group, device number, block size and attribute flags. A portable time value pairs a signed seconds field with an unsigned nanosecond field and a reserved field.

An extended status record carries a validity mask, block size, attribute bits, link count, user and group, mode with spare, inode, size, block count, attribute mask, four portable times for access, birth, change and modification, device and filesystem major and minor numbers, and trailing spare. A filesystem statistics record carries block, free, available, file and free file counts, block size, name length, fragment size, padding and spare. A file lock range carries start, end, type and owning thread group.
The wire protocol reports major version seven and minor version forty six, with the root directory fixed as identifier one.

Attribute update selection uses bit zero for mode through bit eleven for kill privileged bits, covering user, group, size, access time, modification time, handle, immediate access and modification times, lock owner, change time and privileged bit handling in order. Open behavior uses bit zero for direct input output through bit eight for io uring zero copy, covering cache retention, non seekable, directory caching, streaming, no flush, parallel direct writes, passthrough and zero copy in order.

Low capability bits run from zero for asynchronous read through thirty one reserved, including posix locks, file operations, atomic truncate, export, large writes, no masking, splice write, splice move, splice read, flock locks, ioctl direction, automatic invalidation, readdirplus use, automatic readdirplus, asynchronous direct input output, writeback cache, no open support, parallel directory operations, privileged bit handling, access control lists, abort error, maximum pages, symlink caching, no opendir, explicit invalidation, mapping alignment, submounts, second privileged handling, extended attribute extension and extension flag in order.

High capability bits continue from thirty two for security context through forty three for io uring buffer pool, including inode direct access, supplementary group creation, expire only, direct input output with mapping, passthrough, no export, resend, identity mapping, io uring transport and request timeout in order. A relaxed direct input output name aliases the mapping allowance.

Per operation options use small bit numbers. Release distinguishes flush one and flock unlock two. Attribute fetch, file locking, poll scheduling, sync selection, submount marking, open privileged handling, extended attribute privileged handling and expiry selection each use bit zero or bit one as documented, with direct access as bit one in attribute flags. Write cache control uses cache one, lock owner two and privileged kill four, with a privileged alias equal to the kill value. Read lock ownership is two. Ioctl control uses compat one, unrestricted two, retry four, thirty two bit eight, direction sixteen and extended compat thirty two, with at most two hundred fifty six vector entries. Character device extension unrestricted ioctl is one.

The request set defines lookup one, forget two with no reply, getattr three, setattr four, readlink five, symlink six, mknod eight, mkdir nine, unlink ten, rmdir eleven, rename twelve, link thirteen, open fourteen, read fifteen, write sixteen, statfs seventeen, release eighteen, fsync twenty, setxattr twenty one, getxattr twenty two, listxattr twenty three, remove xattr twenty four, flush twenty five, init twenty six, opendir twenty seven, readdir twenty eight and releasedir twenty nine.

The request set continues with fsyncdir thirty, get lock thirty one, set lock thirty two, blocking set lock thirty three, access thirty four, create thirty five, interrupt thirty six, block map thirty seven, destroy thirty eight, ioctl thirty nine, poll forty, notify reply forty one, batch forget forty two, fallocate forty three, readdirplus forty four, second rename forty five, seek forty six, copy range forty seven, setup mapping forty eight, remove mapping forty nine, syncfs fifty, temporary file fifty one, statx fifty two and sixty four bit copy fifty three, plus character device init at four thousand ninety six. Two large reserved values encode byte order detection. Notifications run poll one through prune nine. Extension typing reserves zero through thirty one for security context with maximum thirty one and groups at thirty two.

Entry lookup reply carries node identity, generation, name and attribute cache durations with nanosecond parts, plus full attributes. Forget input carries only a lookup count, single forget adds node identity, batch forget carries a count with padding. Attribute fetch input carries option flags, padding and handle. Attribute reply carries cache duration with nanosecond part, padding and attributes. Extended status fetch carries option flags, reserved space, handle and status mask and flags, with reply carrying cache duration, flags, spare and extended status.

Creation inputs carry mode with device or mask values, with rename carrying a new parent and extended rename adding flags and padding, and link carrying an existing node. Attribute update input carries a validity mask, padding, handle, size, lock owner, three times with nanosecond parts, mode, user and group with unused slots. Open and create inputs carry flags with open behavior bits, create adding mode and mask, with open reply returning handle, behavior bits and backing identity. Release and flush carry handle with flags or lock owner, read and write carry handle, offset, size, operation flags, lock owner and extra flags with padding, write reply returning accepted size.

Filesystem status reply wraps the statistics record. Sync input carries handle with sync flags and padding. Extended attribute set carries size, flags, operation flags and padding, fetch carries size with padding and reply returns size. Lock exchange carries handle, owner, range and option flags with padding, reply returning the range, while access check carries a mask with padding. Initialization exchanges carry major, minor, readahead and capability words with reserved space, reply adding background limits, congestion limit, write size, time granularity, page limits, alignment, extended capabilities, stack depth, timeout and spare. Character device initialization mirrors version and flags with read and write limits, device numbers and spare. Remaining controls cover interrupt identity, block mapping, ioctl handle with command and transfer sizes plus vector base and length with result and vector counts, poll handle with flags and events plus returned events and wakeup handle, and fallocate handle with offset, length, mode and padding.

Every request header carries total length, operation number, unique identity, target node, caller user, group and process identifiers, extension length in eight byte units, and padding. Every reply header carries total length, signed error and matching unique identity. A directory entry carries inode number, offset, name length, entry type and a trailing variable length name.

Compatibility sizes are entry reply one hundred twenty, attribute reply ninety six, mknod input eight, write input twenty four, status size forty eight, extended attribute set input eight, init reply eight and older init reply twenty four. Minimum read buffer is eight thousand one hundred ninety two and character device init information is bounded by four thousand ninety six. Invalid user and group is all bits set in thirty two bits. Resend is indicated by the top bit of the sixty four bit unique identity.

Several values are defined by combination or equality rather than independently. The compatibility request mask is the union of sync and extended attribute. The full raw command size adds command size, one count byte and reply size. Network and link packet offsets each have an alias with identical value. Relaxed direct input output aliases the mapping allowance, and privileged write kill aliases the suid kill value. Reserved initialization markers are the character device init shifted by eight and the init operation shifted by twenty four for endian detection.

Several interfaces require careful length and lifetime handling. The floppy descriptor mixes user and kernel addresses with separate transfer, physical and buffer lengths and in kernel chaining, and allows command bytes to extend into reply space for long commands. The mapping reply and directory entry end in variable arrays whose allocation must use the capacity count and name length rather than the header size. The filter program header carries a user pointer with a cell count. Request extension length is counted in eight byte units, unique identities reserve the top bit for resend, and invalid identity uses all bits set, so equality checks must account for those encodings. Forget has no reply and several compatibility sizes differ from native sizes, so version handling must not assume fixed lengths.
